newsitem.title: USA: Finance officers urge more changes in stadium bill.
newsitem.headline: Finance officers urge more changes in stadium bill.

text.p: A hundred finance officers from across New York State thanked U.S. Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan for delaying the effective date in his controverial stadium bond bill, but said more changes are needed now.
"Your recent statement revising the effective date of this bill is an important development," the officials said in a one-page letter to Moynihan, D-NY.
But the joint letter says the bill's definition of "professional sports facilities" is too broad and the bill would hike borrowing costs for capital improvements at existing facilities.
"S.1880 would affect a great many facilities that are not the stadium financings making headlines," says the letter, spearheaded by the Government Finance Officers Association.
"Included are community stadiums and recreational facilities only sometimes used by professional athletes, such as minor league baseball teams," the letter says.
"We urge you to modify the substantive provisions of your legislation before its reintroduction next year," the officials said.
A Moynihan spokesman was unavailable for comment.
